source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
scope: Additive 1999 flora morphology and documented historical synonyms; preserve old records/photos/attributions; defer BONAP county review.

morphology.habit: Clump-forming or rhizomatous perennial, 40–150 cm tall
morphology.leaves: Alternate, middle blades lanceolate/narrowly ovate 3.7–17 × 2–6 cm; underside sparse pubescence to tomentose with curled hairs
morphology.stems: Usually curly spreading hairs, sometimes requiring lens
morphology.phyllaries: Outer smaller; middle have shiny resin glands and acute/acuminate outward-curving or spreading tips
morphology.heads: Discoid, no rays, generally 9–34 purple tubular florets in 2–6 mm-wide involucres per key
morphology.fruits: Fine ribbed cypselae; genus has abundant long barbellate pappus bristles plus small outer scales

notes: Resiniferous phyllary glands and curling abaxial leaf hairs differentiate V. baldwinii from V. gigantea sensu 1999 flora.

morphology.leaves: Narrowly linear, densely white-woolly abaxial leaf blade, alternate cauline foliage
morphology.phyllaries: Backs of phyllaries appressed white/gray pubescent
morphology.heads: Purple discoid flowerheads without ray florets, in clusters per genus
morphology.fruits: Genus long scabrous pappus plus small scales

notes: The strongly white-woolly leaf undersides and stems are critical photo targets; use against V. baldwinii and hybrid.

morphology.habit: Perennial hybrid described from crossing V. baldwinii and V. lindheimeri in historical flora
morphology.leaves: Undersides gray-green, thinly pubescent to nearly glabrous, versus dense white wool of V. lindheimeri
morphology.phyllaries: Backs with appressed pubescence similar to V. lindheimeri
morphology.flowers: Purple disk-only florets and bristly pappus per genus
morphology.habitat: Historical herbarium specimens noted from Dallas and Bell County

notes: No independent height, flowering period or fruit metrics in historical hybrid account; do not inherit measurements from either parent.
Hybrid identity requires specimen-context support, not just one intermediate leaf.

morphology.leaves: Opposite below, alternate above; ovate or rhombic-ovate with cuneate/truncate bases and serrate edges
morphology.phyllaries: Three overlapping ranks, hard ovate bases and narrow leafy linear tips
morphology.heads: 10–12 yellow pistillate infertile rays, ligules ~7–15 × 3–7.5 mm
morphology.fruits: Black/mottled appressed-hairy cypselae ~3.5–4 mm; 2 pappus awns 2.2–2.8 mm and four fringed small scales

notes: Modern POWO continues to accept Viguiera dentata (Cav.) Spreng.; avoid automatically changing to Aldama dentata, which may represent a different author/concept.

morphology.habit: Small coarse-hairy shrub about 0.5–1 m high (historical Texas taxon concept)
morphology.leaves: Opposite sessile, narrowly ovate, usually ≥5 cm, tapered base, coarsely toothed or slightly lobed
morphology.heads: Long-peduncled solitary or groups of three, phyllaries in two series
morphology.fruits: Two- or three-angled typically winged cypselae; 2–3 short pappus awns with short hyaline scales

notes: Historical 1999 flora explicitly states older usage W. acapulcensis var. hispida 'of authors, not (Kunth) Strother'. This conflicts with modern Kew/ITIS placing W. texana as synonym of W. acapulcensis var. hispida. Taxonomic concept reconciliation needed.

Crosswalk supported by https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/967065-1 and https://itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?print_version=PRT&search_topic=TSN&search_value=780980&source=to_print; use local UT description for modern variety-specific details.

records.original_flora_name: Xanthium strumarium L. var. canadense (Mill.) Torr. & A.Gray

morphology.habit: Coarse monoecious taprooted annual usually 0.4–2 m
morphology.leaves: Alternate, rough-textured, ovate/deltoid/kidney-shaped to 15 cm long, toothed/shallow lobed, truncate or heart-shaped bases, petioles up to 15 cm; no nodal spines
morphology.male_heads: Small staminate heads, separate phyllaries, 5 free anthers
morphology.female_heads: Axillary fertile heads with phyllaries fused to form prickly burr enclosing two flowers without corollas
morphology.fruit: Each burr contains two cypselae; mature burr ~ (1–)2–3+ cm long × ~1.5 cm across, two terminal beaks and numerous ~5 mm hooked prickles
morphology.habitat: Moist disturbed ground and sandy soils

historical_synonyms: Xanthium italicum Moretti [historic var. canadense synonym]
notes: The 1999 flora explicitly warns X. strumarium is extremely variable and its infraspecific divisions uncertain.
Do not project var. canadense measurements across all current broad species without source review.
Seeds and seedlings can be toxic to livestock; avoid safety claims from photos alone.

holds.name: Wedelia acapulcensis
holds.reason: Modern broad species record needs separate FNA/POWO/field account; do not assume historic W. texana describes all varieties.

holds.name: Wedelia acapulcensis var. hispida
holds.reason: 1999 author says W. texana not identical to usages of var. hispida, but current Kew/ITIS synonymize; reconcile author-concept before changing learner.
